in_arabic.name: عوفا
in_arabic.meaning: اسم عربي يرمز للعفة والإنضباط والصبر
in_arabic.long_meaning: يعود اسم عوفا إلى أصل عربي يرمز للأنضباط والصبر والصالحية، وقد تم اختياره من قبل العديد من المسلمين لتمثيل قيمهم الدينية، ويتميز اسم عوفا بالعفة والانتماء للدين، ويعد من أسماء الرجال في الإسلام التي تميزها الصبر والانضباط.

in_urdu.name: عوفا
in_urdu.meaning: نام جوڑا کہ عفت اور انضباط کا مظاہرہ کرتا ہے
in_urdu.long_meaning: عوفا نام کا تعلق عربي زبان سے ہے، جس کے معنی عفت اور انضباط کے ہیں، یہ نام پاکستان میں زیادہ استعمال ہوتا ہے، اس نام کے بارے میں یہ مانا جاتا ہے کہ وہ شخص جو کہ عفت اور انضباط کا مظاہرہ کرتا ہے وہی عوفا ہے، اس نام کی قدیم تاریخ ہے، یہ نام بے شمار لوگوں کے لئے نام رکھنے کا منصوبہ بنایا گیا ہے۔

The name Aufa is also associated with the concept of 'isma', which refers to the ability to control one's desires and impulses. In modern times, the name Aufa is used in many Muslim cultures, and it is seen as a symbol of self-control and discipline.

historical_references.reference: Aufa bint As-Sa'd ibn al-Ashjar was the wife ofAli ibn Abi Talib and the mother of Hassan and Husayn. She is known for her piety and devotion to the Prophet Muhammad. Aufa is mentioned in several Hadiths, including one where she interceded on behalf of the Muslims to the Prophet, asking him to pray for forgiveness for them. Another Hadith relates that when the Prophet was on his deathbed, he requested that Aufa be present to comfort him and recite the Quran to him.
historical_references.time_period: 614-661 CE, during the lifetime of Prophet Muhammad and after his death until the caliphate of Ali ibn Abi Talib.
historical_references.context: Marriage and bereavement of Ali ibn Abi Talib; intercession and comfort during the Prophet's last days

historical_references.reference: Aufa bint Umar was a prominent female companion of the Prophet Muhammad. She was a sister of Umar ibn Al-Khattab, the second caliph of Islam. Aufa is known for her piety and her generosity towards the poor. She was one of the first women to accept Islam and was a close friend of Aisha bint Abu Bakr, the wife of the Prophet Muhammad. Aufa is mentioned in various Hadiths, including one where she gave her ring to the Prophet as a gift and he returned it to her, saying that it would bring her blessings.
historical_references.time_period: 622-632 CE, during the early years of Islam in Medina.
historical_references.context: Acceptance of Islam and generosity towards the poor
